subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw add a versioned core/plugin response-gate API that can fail closed before final response or public-action delivery, and what validator/tool-accounting/audit semantics should be in the first supported contract?
rationale: The remaining work changes a security boundary and product contract across final response delivery, plugin APIs, config/defaults, retry/fallback behavior, and audit logs; automation cannot choose those semantics safely.

options.title: Design response-gate API first
options.body: Approve a focused design pass for mandatory tool-call accounting, typed response validators, fail-closed fallback modes, bounded retries, and audit records before any implementation PR.

options.title: Limit to existing plugin hooks
options.body: Keep domain policies in current plugins and document that OpenClaw does not yet provide a hard final-response gate, leaving this issue open or deferring it explicitly.

options.title: Split narrower security items
options.body: Move public-action approval and outbound pre-send enforcement to narrower issues while keeping this issue as the umbrella response-gate contract discussion.

recommendation.title: Design response-gate API first
recommendation.body: Approve a focused design pass for mandatory tool-call accounting, typed response validators, fail-closed fallback modes, bounded retries, and audit records before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc introduced the closest current finalization hook and has the strongest feature-history link to the plugin API surface that would need extension.
